clue.text: Place to sleep for daughter in town

parts.note: a bed is where you sleep
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone is looking for a bed for their daughter in some town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' reads as a preposition in the surface but is simply kept as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedford is the county town of Bedfordshire in England.

clue.text: Fertilizer, one Mabel spread outside

indicators.note: spread out over the ground means scattered about, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener called Mabel is spreading fertilizer outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonemeal is ground animal bone used as a slow-release garden fertilizer.

clue.text: Sweet character penning boy a farewell note

indicators.note: to pen something is to enclose it, as in a sheep pen

parts.note: sweet in the sense of lovable, dear
a character of the alphabet is a letter

explanation.surface: A sweet person writes a goodbye note to a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing, fitting the note, but signals enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dear John letter is one ending a romantic relationship, a breakup note.

clue.text: Working with sailor, one round lake

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
tar is old slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor working a boat goes once round a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Ontario is the smallest of North America's Great Lakes.

clue.text: Doctor's bad practice

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor; the 's joins
ill can mean bad, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A doctor is accused of poor medical practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'practice' looks like a medical practice but means repeated exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a routine exercise rehearsed to build skill, a kind of practice.

clue.text: Pollster in Missouri State

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for Missouri
RI is Rhode Island, another US state

explanation.surface: A polling company is operating in the state of Missouri.
explanation.walkthrough: MORI was a well-known British opinion-polling firm, now part of Ipsos.
explanation.definitionFit: MORI (Market and Opinion Research International) conducted British opinion polls, making it a pollster.

clue.text: Wild animals go in trees

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Wild creatures disappear into the woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnolias are flowering trees and shrubs with large showy blooms.

clue.text: Feeling of guilt about son breaking and entering again

indicators.note: a burglar breaking and entering goes inside a building, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A burglar regrets his son breaking in for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking and entering' is the legal phrase for burglary; read as the instruction to put one letter inside a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret for a wrong one has done, the sensation of guilt.

clue.text: Abusive about a video that advertises adhesive material

indicators.note: one word placed about another surrounds it

explanation.surface: An offensive promotional video for some sticky product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that advertises' merely pretends the video is an advert, linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulating tape is a sticky electrical tape used to cover wires.

clue.text: Was first to engage a guide

indicators.note: to engage someone is to take them on, holding them within

parts.note: whoever was first led the field

explanation.surface: Someone got in first to hire a tour guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead is someone or something that shows the way, as a guide does.

clue.text: The gin ran out? Something only just avoided

indicators.note: something that has run out is gone or disordered, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: The bar has run out of gin, a narrowly escaped disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a narrow escape, an outcome barely avoided.

clue.text: Piece of coal in colliery cut into small pieces

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a colliery is a coal mine

indicators.note: only a piece of the following word is taken, here its opening letter

explanation.surface: A lump of coal at the pit is chopped into small bits.
explanation.definitionFit: To mince food is to chop or grind it finely.

clue.text: Army officer, the elder of two brothers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the rank above captain
second meaning: in British public schools the older of two brothers was called Smith ...

explanation.walkthrough: British boarding schools traditionally distinguished brothers as 'major' (older) and 'minor' (younger).
explanation.definitionFit: Major is both a military rank and an old school label attached to the surname of the senior sibling.

clue.text: Inspect butcher's circular

explanation.surface: Someone is checking a meat shop's advertising leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'have a butcher's' (butcher's hook) means have a look.
explanation.definitionFit: To look round a place is to tour it and examine it, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Awful hardship, so real in a volume of poetry

indicators.note: something awful is in a terrible state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A book of poems depicts terrible, very real hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: Shropshire is a rural English county; A.E. Housman's poems are full of its young men's hardship and death.
explanation.definitionFit: A Shropshire Lad is A. E. Housman's 1896 collection of poems, a famous single book of verse.

clue.text: Wine — review one's limit

indicators.note: re-view, to look again from a different angle, so the letters are seen in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A wine critic reconsiders how much they can drink.
explanation.definitionFit: St-Émilion is a red Bordeaux from the town of that name in south-west France.

clue.text: Everyone at that place is completely sane

explanation.surface: Everybody present at some location is perfectly rational.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'all there' is an idiom for being mentally alert and of sound mind.

clue.text: Dog moves awkwardly where there's new pelican crossing

indicators.note: to cross something is to straddle it, with a part on each side
a new version of the word that follows is a remade arrangement of its letters

parts.note: to lumber is to move heavily and clumsily

explanation.surface: A dog shambles about at a new pedestrian crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: A pelican crossing is a British pedestrian crossing with push-button lights, which makes 'crossing' look like part of a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The clumber spaniel is a heavy, slow-moving gundog breed named after Clumber Park.

clue.text: Mum on trial after break-up of marriage

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sitting on another comes before it

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: after a break-up the pieces are scattered, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A mother faces court once her marriage has collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital means relating to marriage or to husband and wife.

clue.text: Wary about book on a part of Canada

indicators.note: in a down entry, the piece placed on another sits above it, so comes first
going about something means encircling it

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Someone is cautious about a book on a region of Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Alberta is one of the provinces of western Canada.

clue.text: Gloomy? Sunnier at resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, to sort over again, which puts the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Is a holidaymaker gloomy even though it is sunnier at the seaside resort?
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but is read as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a dark, sullen temperament, once blamed on the planet Saturn's influence.

clue.text: Cashier in bed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the verb to cashier, dismiss from service
second meaning: informal word for bed, as in hit the hay

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashier' looks like a bank teller but is the verb meaning to dismiss someone, especially an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack is to fire someone, and 'the sack' is slang for one's bed.

clue.text: English Opening in tournament

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: The English Opening, a chess move, is played in a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: The English Opening is a real chess opening, so the surface hides two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a single sporting competition, the sort that makes up a tournament.

clue.text: Large hospital at end of that wide bay

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

explanation.surface: A big hospital stands at the far side of a broad bay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bight is a long, gently curving indentation in a coastline, a broad open bay.

clue.text: Talk about Ecstasy con

indicators.note: going about something means surrounding it on all sides

parts.note: E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug-related scam is under discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: To con someone is to swindle or deceive them, which is a synonym of cheat.

clue.text: Make drunk, mixing a beer in it

indicators.note: mixing stirs things together, so the letters lose their order

explanation.surface: A cocktail with beer added will get you intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'in' belongs to the fodder; the first is just joining.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, inebriate means to intoxicate someone with alcohol.

clue.text: Info wanted about lake in valley

indicators.note: one thing going about another wraps right round it

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, the kind someone wants
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone is asking for details about a loch in a Scottish valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, especially in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: No trouble, we hear, landing on net from swing

indicators.note: one piece landing on another is set after it in a down-the-page order
what we hear is spoken, so the words before are taken by sound

parts.note: doing something with ease is doing it with no trouble

explanation.surface: An acrobat lands safely in the safety net after leaving the swing.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a horizontal bar hung on ropes, an acrobat's swing.
